source.author: verg
source.text: Postquam res Asiae Priamique evertere gentem immeritam visum Superis, ceciditque superbum Ilium, et omnis humo fumat Neptunia Troia, diversa exsilia et desertas quaerere terras auguriis agimur divom, classemque sub ipsa Antandro et Phrygiae molimur montibus Idae, incerti, quo fata ferant, ubi sistere detur, contrahimusque viros.
source.text_original: Postquam res Asiae Priamique evertere gentem / immeritam visum Superis, ceciditque superbum / Ilium, et omnis humo fumat Neptunia Troia, / diversa exsilia et desertas quaerere terras / auguriis agimur divom, classemque sub ipsa / Antandro et Phrygiae molimur montibus Idae, / incerti, quo fata ferant, ubi sistere detur, / contrahimusque viros.
source.text_english: After it seemed good to the gods to overthrow the affairs of Asia and Priam’s undeserving people, and proud Ilium had fallen, and all Neptune’s Troy was smoking on the ground, we were driven by the omens of the gods to seek out scattered exiles and deserted lands, and we set about our fleet at Antandros itself and beneath the mountains of Phrygian Ida, unsure where the fates would carry us or where we would be allowed to settle, and we gathered our men together.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: moliri hunc puppem iubet et demittere ferro robora, Peliacas et iam comes exit in umbras.
reuse.text_original: moliri hunc puppem iubet et demittere ferro / robora, Peliacas et iam comes exit in umbras.
reuse.text_english: He orders this ship to be launched and the timbers to be cut down with iron, and as companion he already goes forth into the shades of Pelias.
